trial_court: Principal Judge, Family Court, Ludhiana, T.A.No. 1464 of 2022 (O&M)
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Parties were married in 2018 and have a 2-year-old child. Petitioner-wife is living separately since 2021 and seeking transfer of respondent-husband's petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, pending before Ludhiana court.

legal_principles.principle: The ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit.
legal_principles.held: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. Saravana Karthik (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both parties.
legal_principles.held: In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose protective umbrella they are seeking their sustenance to life.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. Saravana Karthik (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: Generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer.
legal_principles.held: Given the prevailing socioeconomic paradigm in the Indian society, generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. Saravana Karthik (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

outcome.final_order: Case transferred to a Court of competent jurisdiction at Samana, District Patiala.
